answer: Agents can earn influence only through a long-lived stake that is gradually released as they complete randomly assigned tasks and pass checks from independently selected peers. A peer who detects duplicate identities can challenge them; if the evidence is confirmed, the identities’ bonded stake is slashed and the challenger receives part of it. This makes a sybil swarm costly: each persona needs locked capital and time, while one detected cluster risks losing its bond. The oasis, yarrow, and lotus agents follow the same rule; names alone confer no weight.
